Field.name: WatchDirectory
Field.usage: Directory in which to find Alignframes command files or stacks
Field.manpage: Directory to watch for Alignframes(1) command files, whose extension should be .pcm, or stacks, whose extension should be .mrc or .tif.

Field.name: OutputDirectory
Field.usage: Directory in which to write aligned sums and other output
Field.manpage: Directory in which to write aligned sums and other output. This directory must already exist. By default, files are written to the command file directory.

Field.name: ProcessedDirectory
Field.usage: Directory into which finished frame stacks will be moved
Field.manpage: One or more directories into which frame stacks will be moved when they are finished being processed. If a relative path is entered, it will be treated as relative to the watched directory, not the current directory. The directory will be created if it does not exist. If multiple directories are entered, the program will cycle through them. When a command file to process a single frame file is done, the program will move the stack, command file, and log file into the directory. If this directory is on another filesystem, the files will be copied there and deleted from their current location. If the command file has options to use a gain reference file or a defect correction file, copies of these files will also be maintained in the processed directory. Alternatively, when moving files without a command file, the program will look for the names of the gain and defect files in the stack header and make sure there are copies of those. When a command file to process a whole tilt series is done, nothing is moved unless the last component of the path to the frame files is the same as the tilt series root name. SerialEM will write files in this way if the option to use the file name of the current open file in the name of the frame stack folder is selected in the Frame File Options dialog. In that case, the directory itself is moved to the processed directory, since it can be assumed not to contain other frame stacks to be processed. If this \fB-processed\fR option is not entered, the program will just rename each ".pcm" file used to align the frames to "...pcm.done".

Field.name: MasterCommandFile
Field.usage: Name of command file to use if watching for frame stacks
Field.manpage: Name of a command file to use if watching for frame stacks instead ".pcm" files. For each stack, the entries will be modified appropriately, a file will be written with the root name of the stack plus ".pcm", and that file will be run. This master file should have either commands to run Alignframes(1) (including lines with the options "InputFile" and "OutputImageFile") or entries INPUTFILE and OUTPUTFILE that will be substituted with the names of the frame stack and aligned sum file, respectively. If a file contains Alignframes(1) options to apply a gain reference or defect file, the specified files will be used without any checking for whether there is a newer file that applies to the current frames. Thus, be sure these entries are correct for the current session before using a command file with such entries.

Field.name: NoCommandFile
Field.usage: Just watch for frame stacks without a command file to run
Field.manpage: Just watch for frame stacks without running a command file. This option cannot be entered with \fB-master\fR and must be accompanied by either \fB-processed\fR, \fB-before\fR, or \fB-after\fR; i.e., there must be something for the program to do with each stack. If a command file does exist with the same root name as the stack, it will be copied also.

Field.name: ExcludeFilesMatching
Field.usage: When watching for stacks, exclude file names containing given string
Field.manpage: When watching for stacks, exclude file names containing the given string. This option can be used to exclude the frame stacks when processing whole tilt series with an .mdoc file containing frame file names.

Field.name: MdocLacksImageExt
Field.usage: The .mdoc file names do not include the image file extension
Field.manpage: When watching for stacks, .mdoc file names will be derived from the root name of the stack instead of the full name with extension (e.g., setname.mdoc instead of setname.mrc.mdoc).

Field.name: FrameFilesInMdoc
Field.usage: Use names of frame stacks from an .mdoc file
Field.manpage: Use names of frame stacks from an .mdoc file. This option is useful when watching for tilt series stacks and not doing dose weighting.

Field.name: DropAndReplacementDoses
Field.usage: Threshold dose for excluding frame set and dose to accumulate instead
Field.manpage: Threshold dose for excluding frame set and dose to accumulate instead. This option is appropriate if Alignframes(1) is being run and causes the corresponding option to be inserted into the command file.

Field.name: DropSetIfMeanBelow
Field.usage: Exclude frame sets with mean in .mdoc file below given value
Field.manpage: Exclude frame sets with a mean in an .mdoc file below the given value. This option is appropriate if Alignframes(1) is being run and causes the corresponding option to be inserted into the command file.

Field.name: MinimumAgeOfStacks
Field.usage: Time since last modification of a stack before starting to process it
Field.manpage: When watching for frame stacks, use this option to set the minimum time interval between the last detected change in the modification time of the stack and starting to process the stack. The default is 15 seconds.

Field.name: UseGPU
Field.usage: Use GPU for computation; 0 for best available one or number of GPU
Field.manpage: Use the GPU (graphical processing unit) for computations; enter 0 to use the best GPU on the system, or the number of a specific GPU (numbered from 1). This entry overrides whatever was originally written into the command file.

Field.name: BinningOfSum
Field.usage: Image reduction to apply to summed frames
Field.manpage: Image reduction to apply to summed frames; this will override the value in the command files, which was set from the binning of the image returned to SerialEM.

Field.name: ScalingOfSum
Field.usage: Amount to scale summed values before output
Field.manpage: Amount to scale summed values before output; this will override the value in the command files, which was set to match the scaling of images returned to SerialEM. If dose-weighting is being used without the \fB-dnorm\fR option, additional scaling may be needed to preserve intensity resolution in highly filtered images.

Field.name: DosesInMetadataFile
Field.usage: Do dose weighting with dose values in metadata (.mdoc) file
Field.manpage: Do dose weighting with dose values in metadata file, if it is present. This entry will lead to an entry "TypeOfDoseFile 4" in the ".pcm" file and remove entries for FixedTotalDose or FixedFrameDoses. When frames sets are being aligned for a whole tilt series, the metadata file entry is already present in the ".pcm" file. In other cases, the program will look for a frame stack .mdoc file, i.e., a file with ".mdoc" appended to the name of the input stack. If this file is present, the MetadataFile option will be added to the ".pcm" file; otherwise nothing will be added. This option cannot be entered with \fB-dframe\fR or \fB-dtotal\fR.

Field.name: FixedTotalDose
Field.usage: Total dose for each set of frames, in electrons/square Angstrom
Field.manpage: Total dose for each set of frames (not for entire tilt series), in electrons/square Angstrom. This entry will lead to a corresponding entry in the ".pcm" file, replacing an existing one if any, and remove entries for TypeOfDoseFile or FixedFrameDoses. This option cannot be entered with \fB-dmdoc\fR or \fB-dframe\fR.

Field.name: FixedFrameDoses
Field.usage: List of frame doses and numbers that applies to all frame sets
Field.manpage: List of frame doses and numbers that applies to all sets of frames. The list is a set of paired numbers: a dose in electrons/square Angstrom and the number of frames taken at that dose (e.g., enter "2,10,4,5" for 10 frames of 2 e/A^2 and 5 frames of 4 e/A^2). This entry will lead to a corresponding entry in the ".pcm" file, replacing an existing one if any, and remove entries for TypeOfDoseFile or FixedTotalDose. This option cannot be entered with \fB-dmdoc\fR or \fB-dtotal\fR.

Field.name: InitialPriorDose
Field.usage: Dose applied before any of the images in each frame set were taken
Field.manpage: Dose applied before any of the images in each frame set were taken; this value will lead to a corresponding entry in the ".pcm" file, replacing an existing one if any.

Field.name: NormalizeDoseWeighting
Field.usage: Normalize the dose weight filters to sum to 1 within each frame set
Field.manpage: Normalize the dose weight filters so that they add up to to 1.0 within each set of frames. This entry will lead to a corresponding entry in the ".pcm" file. It is useful for tilt series where dose weighting of the tilt images is to be done in a later step.

Field.name: UnweightedFileSuffix
Field.usage: Suffix for output file with non-dose weighted summed images
Field.manpage: Suffix for name of output file of summed images that have not been dose weighted, created in addition to the dose-weighted images placed in the main output file. The file will be named with _suffix.mrc after the stack root name.

Field.name: Voltage
Field.usage: Microscope voltage in kV; must be either 200 or 300
Field.manpage: Microscope voltage in kV; this value must be either 200 or 300. This entry will lead to a corresponding entry in the ".pcm" file, replacing an existing one if any; if none is entered, the default in Alignframes(1) is 300 kV.

Field.name: DriftLimitDistAndNumber
Field.usage: Shift above which to drop initial frames, and max # or fraction to drop
Field.manpage: Maximum shift between frames above which to drop initial frames of the set (in unbinned pixels), and either the maximum fraction or the maximum number of frames to drop. This entry will lead to a corresponding entry in the ".pcm" file. It is particularly useful for single-exposure (frame) tilt series.

Field.name: ReducedSum
Field.usage: Image reduction or target size for small copy of sum
Field.manpage: Amount to reduce image by, or target size, to get a reduced copy of the summed image. A value of 32 or less will be taken as the shrinkage factor, and a value greater than 32 will be taken as the target size to shrink too. In the latter case, the geometric mean of the X and Y size will be divided by the target size and rounded to an integer. The output file will be named as the stack root name followed by "_redN.mrc", where N is the reduction factor. The file will be placed in the same directory as the aligned sum unless a different destination is specified with the \fB-thumb\fR option. If the summed file is a tilt series, only the middle image will be used.

Field.name: PowerSpectrum
Field.usage: Height for JPEG of side-by-side reduced sum and power spectrum
Field.manpage: Height for a JPEG file with a side-by-side reduced sum and reduced power spectrum. The summed image will be reduced by exactly the amount to give the specified height. The power spectrum will be computed on the full-sized summed image and reduced to the given height, so it shows all the frequencies in the summed image. The output file will be named as the stack root name followed by "_power.jpg". The file will be placed in the same directory as the aligned sum unless a different destination is specified with the \fB-thumb\fR option. If the summed file is a tilt series, only the middle image will be used.

Field.name: ScaleSpectrum
Field.usage: Background gray level and saturated annulus diameter for spectrum
Field.manpage: Background gray level near the edge of the power spectrum, and the relative diameter of the annulus around the center whose mean will be scaled to be white. The default gray level is 48, and the default diameter is 0.02. Making the diameter smaller will saturate less area at the center of the power spectrum; making it bigger may give more dynamic range to show Thon rings away from the center.

Field.name: ThumbnailDirectory
Field.usage: Directory to place small sum or power spectrum into
Field.manpage: Directory into which the reduced sums or power spectra will be written. If this option is not entered, they will be placed in the same directory as the aligned sums. The directory will be created if it does not exist.

Field.name: RunCommandBefore
Field.usage: Command to run before a command file, if any
Field.manpage: Command to run before running a command file, if any. The command can include items enclosed in %{...} to be substituted with the actual values for the current frame stack. These items include: ^ %{frameFile} - Frame stack, including original path when watching for ".pcm" files ^ %{outputFile} - Aligned sum output file, including path ^ %{gainReference} - Gain reference file, including path ^ %{defectFile} - Defect file, including path ^ %{rootName} - Root name of command file/stack ^ %{outputDir} - Directory entered with \fB-output\fR, if any ^ %{processedDir} - Directory entered with \fB-processed\fR, if any ^ %{reducedDir} - Directory entered with \fB-thumb\fR, if any ^ The substituted text will be enclosed in double quotes, unless it is a root name with no spaces included. Despite the quotes, it may be possible to concatenate these items with other text (it works in Linux). The output file will not exist when a command is run before a command file.

Field.name: RunCommandAfter
Field.usage: Command to run after a command file, if any
Field.manpage: Command to run after running a command file, if any. The command can include the items enclosed in %{...} just described. This command will be run after any moving or renaming of processed files, so the input stack may no longer exist by the same name.

Field.name: TextForNone
Field.usage: Text to substitute in command if file or directory is unavailable
Field.manpage: Text to substitute in a command entered with \fB-before\fR or \fB-after\fR if the file or directory is not available for a particular item. The default is simply to remove the %{...} item if it has no value. Using a defined text such as "NONE" can make it easier for a script to parse the command, for example, because then each option entered to the script would always be followed by another token instead of a blank.

Field.name: KeepCommandLogs
Field.usage: Keep log files with output from running commands before or after
Field.manpage: Keep log files with output from running commands before or after a command file. The default is to write a log then delete it if there is no error.

Field.name: AvoidWindowsCopy
Field.usage: 1 to not use Robocopy, 2 to not use Xcopy either
Field.manpage: 1 to use Xcopy in Windows instead of Robocopy, or 2 to use neither Xcopy nor Robocopy. In the latter case, Cygwin commands will be used when running through Cygwin or Python commands when running a Windows Python. This option exists because Robocopy can give obscure failures in some cases. Xcopy can do the same operations but is "deprecated". Copies with Cygwin commands may be significantly slower in some cases (e.g., with a 10G network); copies of whole directories through Python may be incredibly slow.

Field.name: NicenessSetting
Field.usage: Priority at which to run jobs (higher is less, default 15)
Field.manpage: Priority at which to run jobs, a number between 1 and 19, where a higher value has lower priority. All values in this range are meaningfully different on Linux or Mac OS X, but they will be translated into a smaller selection of priority levels on Linux. The default is 15.

Field.name: ThreadLimit
Field.usage: Limit on number of threads used for processing
Field.manpage: Limit on number of threads used for processing. This value will be used to set OMP_NUM_THREADS, which sets an upper limit to the number of threads used for operations that are multi-threaded with OpenMP (image reductions, FFTs). This thread number is already limited to the number of real cores when hyperthreading is enabled, but allowing that many threads may be counterproductive when other multi-threaded operations are running. You can determine the number of physical and logical cores by entering "imodqtassist -t" in a terminal.

Field.name: usage
Field.usage: Print help output
